_what: Evidence for the pre-registered API-Football trial decision.
_governing_rule: Assert a non-zero COUNT, never a status code. An HTTP 200 carrying an empty or zeroed payload is a FAILURE.
_how_to_read_this: Every check below was fixed in scripts/verify_apifootball.py before an API key existed. criteria_fingerprint is the sha256 of the criteria block: if it does not match the value committed in that script, the criteria were edited and this run is not a pre-registered result.

criteria.governing_rule: Assert a non-zero COUNT, never a status code. An HTTP 200 carrying an empty or zeroed payload is a FAILURE.

check1_xg_presence.completed_fixture_rule: the most recent fixture with status FT/AET/PEN whose kickoff is at least 24h in the past (so stats have had time to be posted); if no such fixture exists, the most recent FT/AET/PEN fixture, flagged
check1_xg_presence.season_fallback_rule: if the current season has no completed fixture, fall back ONCE to the most recent earlier season the plan lists, and print which season was used
check1_xg_presence.pass_rule: all four leagues yield xG > 0 for BOTH teams

check2_current_season.season_derivation: calendar-derived, not provider-declared: split_year leagues -> year if month >= 7 else year - 1; calendar_year leagues -> year
check2_current_season.why_not_provider_declared: the free tier's season list is plan-filtered, so a plan-blind season could flag itself 'current' and pass a check it fails
check2_current_season.pass_rule: len(response) > 0 for every one of the four leagues

check3_identity.team_id_rule: one team, two different fixtures, fetched as two separate /fixtures?id= calls -> the API-Football team id must be identical
check3_identity.player_id_rule: one player present by name in both fixtures' /fixtures/players -> identical player id. No player shared between the two fixtures is INDETERMINATE, which counts as FAIL
check3_identity.ambiguity_rule: any API-Football team resolving to more than one ESPN name, or two API-Football teams claiming the same ESPN name, FAILS EXPLICITLY and is named. An ambiguous identity match must never silently pick a team
check3_identity.min_resolution_rate_rationale: MLS's ESPN reference is operator-curated and slate-verified, so it is held to 100%. The eng.1 / esp.1 / mex.1 ESPN /teams payloads were MEASURED on 2026-07-29 to carry clubs that are not in those top flights and to omit clubs that are, which can account for roughly 20-25% of a roster by itself. 0.75 is the line below which the failure can no longer be blamed on our own stale reference. Both directions are always printed by name so a human attributes each miss rather than reading a percentage
check3_identity.pass_rule: team id stable AND player id stable AND every league at or above its threshold AND zero ambiguous resolutions anywhere

check4_pre_match_leakage.fixture_rule: status.short == 'NS' AND the kickoff timestamp is strictly in the future — the status alone is a provider claim
check4_pre_match_leakage.critical_fail_rule: any xG statistic present with a non-null value other than 0 on a not-started fixture is a CRITICAL FAIL: an xG feature could silently carry the outcome, which this repo treats as a disqualifying defect
check4_pre_match_leakage.observation_rule: a null or exactly-zero pre-match xG placeholder carries no outcome information; it is reported, not failed
check4_pre_match_leakage.empty_response_is: PASS — the single check where an absent payload is the desired result, stated separately from the counts rule on purpose
check4_pre_match_leakage.no_not_started_fixture_found: INDETERMINATE, which counts as FAIL: a leakage check that could not run must never read as clean

overall.DROP: anything else, naming the failing check
